Two people were injured in Iranian attacks on Bahrain on Saturday, including a Bahraini citizen with disabilities whose condition was stable, the Interior Ministry said on Sunday.

The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis toward the Riyadh region, its spokesperson said on Sunday.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Sunday that the country needs lasting deterrence to remove the threat of war.

The UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia condemned Iranian attacks on Bahrain, including an attack on a civilian industrial facility. They expressed solidarity with Bahrain and support for measures to protect its security and sovereignty.

Iran remains in talks with the United States but is prepared for any possible scenario, the deputy foreign minister said on Sunday.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and senior ministers have spent recent weeks preparing for the possibility of renewed US strikes on Iran and their economic consequences, Bloomberg reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the government's thinking.

Iran has banned exports of tomatoes, potatoes and onions following sharp price increases, with authorities seeking to boost domestic supplies of the three widely consumed staples.

The Trade Promotion Organization issued the ban to customs offices following a request from the Agriculture Ministry, with exports suspended until further notice, Iranian media reported Sunday.

Prices have surged in recent weeks, with tomatoes reaching 1.5 million rials per kilogram and potatoes and onions exceeding 1 million rials per kilogram. The continued export of these products amid rising domestic prices has prompted authorities to prioritize supplies for Iranian consumers.

100%Nov 22, 2026, 20:09 GMT+0Police shoot two men after knife attack in Mashhad, one diesOne of two men shot by police after an alleged knife attack that injured three officers in northeastern Iran died after being taken to hospital on Sunday, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported.

Mashhad police chief Alireza Hosseinalizadeh told IRNA that the two men attacked officers with knives near the Azadshahr intersection in Mashhad, prompting police to open fire. Both suspects were shot and detained, while three injured officers were hospitalized.

The circumstances of the incident and the identities of the two men remain unclear.

Arab countries must compensate Iran for war damages, and Tehran should develop nuclear weapons to deter US and Israeli threats, an Iranian lawmaker said Sunday, threatening to use force to recover compensation from Arab states.

Kamran Ghazanfari, a member of parliament's Internal Affairs and Councils Committee, called for Iran to develop nuclear weapons in response to what he described as nuclear threats from the United States and Israel.

"We must move toward revising our nuclear doctrine and equip ourselves with nuclear weapons to defend our people," he told Didban Iran, arguing that such weapons would deter future nuclear threats.

Ghazanfari said Arab countries demanding compensation from Tehran were deluding themselves. "They must pay for all the damage they have caused us, both this year and in previous years. God willing, we will collect every last penny so they never make these mistakes again," he said.

Ghazanfari also demanded the return of Iranian funds frozen in Persian Gulf Arab countries, arguing that negotiations would achieve nothing. "This is a world of force. We must wrest it from their throats through strength and force," he said, calling for a more confrontational approach toward Iran's Arab neighbors.

Turning to Iran's economic crisis, Ghazanfari blamed President Masoud Pezeshkian's government for the collapse of the rial, saying the dollar had risen from 580,000 rials at the beginning of his administration to around 2,700,000 rials, an increase of more than 350 percent.

100%Nov 22, 2026, 17:56 GMT+0Trump leaning toward new Iran strikes after new year - Fox NewsPresident Donald Trump told Fox News on Sunday that he was inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if no deal was reached, and warned that Iranian ships trying to run the US naval blockade would be sunk.

Indirect talks with Tehran were still going on, Trump said, but he called the Iranians "professional tap dancers" who talked constantly without result, Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst reported.

Asked about reports in Iranian state media that Iran planned to test the blockade, Trump said: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy."

Trump also told Yingst he had seen videos of renewed protests in Iran and urged the protesters to keep going.

Iran still has about 1,500 ballistic missiles and can produce about 50 a month, the Wall Street Journal has reported.

Two US aircraft carrier strike groups are operating in the Arabian Sea, and US refueling aircraft are based in Israel, Yingst said. Persian Gulf states, which bore the brunt of Iranian fire during the war, have been urging a negotiated settlement, with Qatar passing messages between Washington and Tehran.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that diplomatic efforts were continuing despite heightened tensions with the United States, according to Iranian media.

Araghchi provided an update on the latest diplomatic developments, emphasizing that "the path of diplomacy continues."

Iranian economist and researcher Mohammad Maljou said he had been sentenced to one year in prison based on his writings and academic activities, adding that he was prevented from speaking at either of his two court hearings.

Maljou said Sunday that interrogators from the Revolutionary Guards' intelligence organization prepared the report used to justify his conviction. The precise criminal charge underlying the sentence has yet to be established.

In November 2025, IRGC intelligence agents searched Maljou's home, confiscated electronic devices and books, and subjected him to three lengthy interrogations. He subsequently announced that he would respond only to judicial authorities.

Seven oil tankers have been struck in the Strait of Hormuz since November 16, including three vessels hit by unidentified projectiles near Oman's coast in a 15-hour period, the Joint Maritime Information Centre said.In its Sunday advisory, distributed by UK Maritime Trade Operations, JMIC said the three latest attacks occurred on November 20 and 21, targeting outbound tankers between 8 and 17 nautical miles from Khasab, Oman. Two of the vessels were struck about 50 minutes apart.

The center reported continued Revolutionary Guards activity involving drone overflights, surveillance of commercial ships and occasional radio warnings. It said Iranian claims that tankers had struck naval mines remained unconfirmed by official authorities.Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely restricted. According to the report, tracking data showed no recorded transits by cargo-carrying vessels above 1,000 deadweight tons between November 19 and 21.

100%Nov 22, 2026, 16:20 GMT+0UKMTO reports military encounter involving tanker in Gulf of OmanThe UK Maritime Trade Operations said Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving an oil tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman.

The maritime security agency said authorities were aware of the incident and investigations were underway. It advised vessels in the area to remain vigilant and monitor the evolving security situation.

UKMTO provided no further details about the incident, including the identity of the tanker or the military forces involved.

100%Nov 22, 2026, 16:15 GMT+0Iran lawmaker urges building nuclear bomb 'once and for all'Iran should build a nuclear bomb once and for all to strengthen its military deterrence against the United States and Israel, a senior Iranian lawmaker said Sunday, calling for a fundamental change in Tehran's nuclear doctrine.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, told the Iranian news outlet Tabnak that US and Israeli attacks had strengthened arguments for developing nuclear weapons, despite warnings from China and Russia against such a move.

"Therefore, it would be better to build and possess a nuclear bomb once and for all to benefit from its deterrence, even if we never use it," he said.

Bakhshayesh Ardestani also said Iran was sending three supertankers to China, warning that a US attack on even one of the tankers would intensify direct military confrontation, adding that Tehran had threatened to strike oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait if its vessels were targeted.

The lawmaker said Iran had overcome weaknesses in its air defenses and air force, improved its radar and surveillance capabilities, and extended its missile range from 2,000 to 4,500 kilometers, bringing US military bases in Europe within reach.

He also argued that Washington could not sustain its costly naval blockade indefinitely, describing the Strait of Hormuz as a powerful strategic weapon and proposing fees or restrictions on ships from countries imposing sanctions on Iran.

100%Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani is the Member of Parliament for Ardestan, a city and county in Iran's Isfahan Province.Nov 22, 2026, 15:55 GMT+0Iran navy says two tankers hit mines, catch fire near HormuzTwo oil tankers caught fire Sunday after striking naval mines in restricted waters east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said in a statement.

The navy said the vessels entered the restricted area despite previous warnings, with their identification and navigation systems switched off.

It warned that shipowners and operators who disregard maritime restrictions would bear responsibility for any resulting damage. The identities of the tankers and the extent of the damage remain unclear.
